page: Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-5760s-amd is an AMD-based server instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, supporting multithreading with 2 threads per core. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 192.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 5760 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong processing capabilities, with both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests placing in the top 25%. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores also rank in the top 25%, showing strong results in image and text processing. Large-block memory bandwidth is a notable highlight, with uncached read-only speeds of 467.73 GB/sec and write speeds of 282.99 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. Conversely, small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth and database operations perform at average levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high resource density by pairing a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with substantial local NVMe storage. This configuration avoids the need for external block storage attachments for large datasets. The hardware is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and data-heavy applications. However, the 2.0 GHz base clock speed represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring extreme single-threaded CPU frequency, though its multi-core performance and memory throughput compensate for this in parallel processing tasks.
